outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Attention and Its Computational Challenges
outline.description: Sets the stage by explaining why attention is central to modern Transformers, its quadratic complexity, and the motivation for faster exact-attention algorithms.
subtopics: Overview of prior acceleration efforts (approximations, software optimizations, alternative architectures)

outline.description: Introduces the GPU execution model, memory hierarchy, and hardware features of NVIDIA Hopper that are essential for FlashAttention‑3.
subtopics: Memory hierarchy: global, L2, shared, registers
Thread hierarchy: threads → warps → warp‑groups → CTAs → clusters
Asynchrony in GPUs: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) and asynchronous Tensor Cores
Low‑precision formats: FP16, BF16, FP8 and their hardware support
Layout constraints for WGMMA (mn‑major vs k‑major) and implications for attention

outline.description: Contrasts naïve attention implementations with the original FlashAttention design, highlighting the memory‑traffic reduction ideas.
subtopics: Standard attention: materializing S and P in global memory
FlashAttention‑1 tiling and kernel fusion concept
FlashAttention‑2 refinements: blockwise processing over Q, K, V dimensions
Limitations of FlashAttention‑2 on Hopper (low utilization, lack of asynchrony/FP8)

outline.description: Detailed walk‑through of the three core techniques that enable the speedup on Hopper GPUs.
subtopics: Hiding Softmax under Asynchronous Block‑wise GEMMs
• Register permutation to match accumulator layout
